rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw in ‘and we glorify’ is circumstantial, like saying, ‘Would you favor someone while I am more deserving of favor?’
rows.anchor: الواو في { ونحن } للحال كما تقول أتحسن إلى فلان وأنا أحق بالإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih and taqdis mean distancing God from what is evil or unfitting.
rows.anchor: والتسبيح تبعيد الله تعالى من السوء وكذا التقديس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terms are associated with swimming in water and traversing land, respectively, in the sense of going through and far away.
rows.anchor: من سبح في الماء وقدس في الأرض إذا ذهب فيها وأبعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Distance from evil is tasbih; distance from good is a curse (laʿn).
rows.anchor: إن أريد به التبعيد عن السوء فهو التسبيح وإن أريد به التبعيد عن الخيرات فهو اللعن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In essence, God is beyond possibility: denying possibility entails denying multiplicity, corporeality, accidents, opposites, and peers, affirming absolute unity and necessary existence.
rows.anchor: أما في الذات فأن لا تكون محلا للإمكان فإن منع السوء وإمكانه هو العدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In attributes, God is free of ignorance and change, encompasses all knowables, and is able to do all that can be done.
rows.anchor: وأما في الصفات فأن يكون منزها عن الجهل فيكون محيطا بكل المعلومات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In acts, God neither seeks benefit nor avoids harm nor gains or loses perfection; he is independent of all existents and nonexistents and sovereign over their creation and annihilation.
rows.anchor: وأما في الأفعال فأن لا تكون أفعاله لجلب المنافع ودفع المضار وأن لا يستكمل بشيء منها

rows.speaker: أهل التذكير
rows.claim: Ahl al-tadhkir say tasbih in the Qur’an can mean transcendence: God has no peer, administers the heavens and worlds, is above wrong descriptions, self-sufficient and sovereign, all-knowing, and without consort or child.
rows.anchor:
قال أهل التذكير :
التسبيح جاء تارة في القرآن بمعنى / التنزيه وأخرى بمعنى التعجب

rows.speaker: أهل التذكير
rows.claim: Ahl al-tadhkir also take tasbih as expressing wonder: at subduing powerful animals for humans, creating without fatigue, teaching without a human teacher, and forgiving long sin after brief repentance.
rows.anchor: أما التعجب فكذلك ( ا ) أنا الذي سخرت البهائم القوية للبشر الضعيف

rows.speaker: أهل التذكير
rows.claim: They urge tasbih for divine favor and relief, including seeking God’s pleasure and praising him morning and evening.
rows.anchor: ثم يقول إن أردت رضوان الله فسبح ، وسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The homily lists tasbih by throne-bearing angels, the close and other angels, prophets, Companions, insects, animals, atoms, and all things in the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: لأن لي من يسبحني ، ومنهم حملة العرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs no creatures’ tasbih; because nonliving things do not need its reward, God gives their reward to the human who serves him, showing that the whole world can be put at the servant’s service.
rows.anchor: أنا الغني عن تسبيح هذه الأشياء ، وهذه الأشياء ليست من الأحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God benefits and purifies the servant, not God; the homily likens the command to a loan that God, though rich, repays tenfold.
rows.anchor: والنكتة الأخرى أذكرني بالعبودية لتنتفع به لا أنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs no army, but promises to help the servant who helps him, although heaven and earth are already his armies.
rows.anchor: كن معينا لي وإن كنت غنيا عن إعانتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs no remembrance because all already remember him, yet remembers the servant who remembers him; he needs no service, since he is king and all creation prostrates, but brief service earns lasting rest.
rows.anchor: ولا حاجة بي إلى ذكرك لأن الكل يذكروني

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf treats ‘with your praise’ as a circumstantial phrase: we glorify you while praising you and clothed in your praise.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) بحمدك في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that glorifying God with praise recognizes that his praise and majesty make him deserving of glorification.
rows.anchor: الأول : أنا إذا سبحناك فنحمدك سبحانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that people can glorify God only through his enabling grace, as David’s example illustrates.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنا نسبحك بحمدك فإنه لولا إنعامك علينا

rows.speaker: داود
rows.claim: David says he cannot thank God, since he can reach gratitude for a blessing only through another blessing; God says recognizing this dependence is gratitude.
rows.anchor: قال داود عليه السلام : يا رب كيف أقدر أن أشكرك

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Dharr asks which utterance God loves most; the Prophet answers that it is what God chose for his angels, ‘Glory and praise be to God’; al-Razi says Muslim recorded it.
rows.anchor: ما اصطفاه الله لملائكته : سبحان الله وبحمد رواه مسلم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr recounts that a hypocrite rebuffed a Muslim who reminded him to pray; ʿUmar struck him, and the Prophet told ʿUmar his anger was honor and his approval judgment.
rows.anchor: وروى سعيد بن جبير قال : ( كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: Gabriel tells the Prophet that angels in the first, second, and third heavens remain prostrating, standing, and bowing, praising God as Lord of dominion, might, and life.
rows.anchor: فأتاه جبريل فقال : يا نبي الله سألك عمر عن صلاة أهل السماء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Masʿud interpret ‘we glorify’ as ‘we pray,’ taking tasbih to mean prayer.
rows.anchor: أي نصلي والتسبيح هو الصلاة ، وهو قول ابن عباس وابن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqdis means purification, as in the expression ‘the Holy Land.’
rows.anchor: التقديس التطهير ، ومنه الأرض المقدسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation addresses God: we declare him purified, describing him with the loftiness and might that befit him.
rows.anchor: أحدها : نطهرك أي نصفك بما يليق بك من العلو والعزة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the angels purify themselves of sins and errors in pursuit of God’s pleasure.
rows.anchor: قول مجاهد نطهر أنفسنا من ذنوبنا وخطايانا ابتغاء لمرضاتك

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says they purify their deeds of sin so the deeds are sincerely for God.
rows.anchor: قول أبي مسلم نطهر أفعالنا من ذنوبنا حتى تكون خالصة لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is purifying the heart of attention to anything besides God until it is absorbed in the lights of knowing him.
rows.anchor: نطهر قلوبنا عن الالتفات إلى غيرك حتى تصير مستغرقة في أنوار معرفتك

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites argue that the angels attribute their glorification and purification to themselves; if God did those deeds, there would be no merit in them over bloodshed.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة هذه الآية تدل على العدل من وجوه : أحدها : قولهم : { ونحن نسبح

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They argue that if God caused corruption and killing, his answer should have been that he owns creation and does as he wills.
rows.anchor: لو كان الفساد والقتل فعلا لله تعالى لكان يجب أن يكون الجواب أن يقول إني مالك أفعل ما أشاء

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They argue that God’s answer disavows corruption and murder, which would be impossible if those acts were his own.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : أن قوله : { أعلم ما لا تعلمون } يقتضي التبري من الفساد

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They ask how God can be praised as transcendent if every indecency, ugliness, injustice, oppression, and corruption is created by his making and will.
rows.anchor: إذا كان لا فاحشة ولا قبح ولا جور ولا ظلم ولا فساد إلا بصنعه وخلقه ومشيئته

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They argue that if God created people for disbelief, his answer should have admitted he created them to corrupt and kill; its refusal supports the Muʿtazilite doctrine of justice.
rows.anchor: لو كان خالقا للكفر لكان خلقهم لذلك الكفر فكان ينبغي أن يكون الجواب نعم خلقهم ليفسدوا وليقتلوا

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They argue that if corruption and killing were God’s acts, they would be like colors and bodies, which are not ordinarily met with wonder.
rows.anchor: وسادسها : لو كان الفساد والقتل ، من فعل الله تعالى لكان ذلك جاريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the Muʿtazilite objections are answered by the arguments about motive and knowledge.
rows.anchor: والجواب عن هذه الوجوه المعارضة بمسألة الداعي والعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer may mean that, despite corruption and killing, God knows there will also be many righteous and devout people among humanity.
rows.anchor: لا تتعجبوا من أن يكون فيهم من يفسد ويقتل فإني أعلم مع هذا بأن فيهم جمعا من الصالحين والمتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the angels were grieving, the answer reassures them that there are many devout people whom God will not disappoint.
rows.anchor: لا تغتموا بسبب وجود المفسدين فإني أعلم أيضا أن فيهم جمعا من المتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the angels ask for the wisdom, God gives the general point; revealing the full detail might itself be harmful.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : أنه طلب الحكمة فجوابه أن مصلحتكم فيه أن تعرفوا وجه الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they are asking to remain in heaven rather than have a human vicegerent on earth, God says their welfare lies in being in heaven, not on earth.
rows.anchor: أنه التماس لأن يتركهم في الأرض وجوابه إني أعلم أن مصلحتكم أن تكونوا في السماء لا في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may be revealing that Iblis is among the angels, with envy, pride, and hypocrisy in his heart.
rows.anchor: وهو أن معكم إبليس وأن في قلبه حسدا وكبرا و نفاقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their self-praise may itself amount to glorifying themselves; later humans will instead humble themselves by confessing wrong and asking mercy.
rows.anchor: فإنكم لما وصفتم أنفسكم بهذه المدائح فقد استعظمتم أنفسكم فكأنكم أنتم بهذا الكلام في تسبيح أنفسكم

none: A standalone verse-text segment with no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sixth favor recalls the demand, the thunderbolt, and revival: God brought them back so they could repent, escape punishment, and gain reward.
rows.anchor: اذكروا نعمتي حين قلتم لموسى لن نؤمن لك حتى نرى الله جهرة فأخذتكم الصاعقة ثم أحييتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story warns Muhammad’s contemporaries against actions that could bring the same punishment upon them.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : أن فيها تحذيرا لمن كان في زمان نبينا محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites’ denial of Moses despite witnessing great signs parallels their descendants’ denial of Muhammad; God withholds comparable signs because their rejection would merit punishment.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : تشبيههم في جحودهم معجزات النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأسلافهم في جحود نبوة موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account consoles Muhammad and steadies him to endure rejection as the resolute messengers endured it.
rows.anchor: ورابعها : فيه تسلية للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مما كان يلاقي منهم وتثبيت لقلبه على الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ancestors’ repeated rejection of Moses despite clear signs answers the claim that scriptural People of the Book should readily accept Muhammad because they knew of him.
rows.anchor: أسلافهم مع مشاهدتهم تلك الآيات الباهرة على نبوة موسى عليه السلام كانوا يرتدون كل وقت ويتحكمون عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad’s accurate telling of these accounts, although he was unlettered and never studied, proves that they came by revelation.
rows.anchor: وسادسها : لما أخبر محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام عن هذه القصص مع أنه كان أميا لم يشتغل بالتعلم

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Moses returned, destroyed the calf, and took seventy chosen men to hear God. A cloud hid Moses; they heard divine commands, then demanded direct sight, died by the thunderbolt, and were revived after Moses prayed.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن اسحاق : لما رجع موسى عليه السلام من الطور إلى قومه

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: In Ibn Ishaq’s account, after the revival Moses asks for Israel’s repentance from calf worship; God requires them to kill themselves as repentance.
rows.anchor: حتى رد الله إليهم أرواحهم وطلب توبة بني إسرائيل من عبادة العجل فقال : لا إلا أن يقتلوا أنفسهم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi places the event after repentance through mutual killing: seventy survivors ask to see God, die, and are revived; learning they had worshipped the calf, they ask Moses to make them prophets and God grants his prayer.
rows.anchor: قال السدي : لما تاب بنو إسرائيل من عبادة العجل بأن قتلوا أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not decide which of the two reported chronologies is correct, or whether the sight-seekers were calf-worshippers or other Israelites.
rows.anchor: ليس في الآية ما يدل على ترجيح أحد القولين على الآخر وكذلك ليس فيها ما يدل على أن الذين سألوا الرؤية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say they will not believe or acknowledge Moses’ prophethood until they see God openly, meaning with their eyes.
rows.anchor: فمعناه لا نصدقك ولا نعترف بنبوتك حتى نرى الله جهرة ( أي ) عيانا

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf analyzes jahratan as a verbal noun from speaking aloud, a kind of seeing treated as a cognate accusative, or a circumstantial accusative meaning openly.
rows.anchor: جهرت بالقراءة وبالدعاء كأن الذي يرى بالعين جاهر بالرؤية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with fatḥa on the hāʾ is reported; jahratan can be a verbal noun like ghalabatan or a plural meaning those who make it manifest.
rows.anchor: وقرىء جهرة بفتح الهاء وهي إما مصدر كالغلبة وإما جمع جاهر

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal derives jahr from manifest appearance, citing uncovering an object, clearing mud from a well until its water appears, a loud voice, and a bright-looking face.
rows.anchor: وقال القفال أصل الجهرة من الظهور يقال جهرت الشيء ( إذا ) كشفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their use of jahratan stresses that they demand visible sight, not knowledge or an imagined vision like one in sleep.
rows.anchor: وإنما قالوا : جهرة تأكيدا لئلا يتوهم متوهم أن المراد بالرؤية العلم أو التخيل

rows.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
rows.claim: Qadi ʿAbd al-Jabbar argues that if seeing God were possible, asking for it would be permissible and should not have brought punishment, just as asking for different food did not.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي عبد الجبار : إنها لو كانت جائزة لكانوا قد التمسوا أمرا مجوزا

words: لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى ٱللَّهَ جَهْرَةًۭ
rows.speaker: أبو الحسين
rows.claim: Abu al-Husayn argues that God presents the demand as grave; if vision were permissible, it would be like asking for a dead person to be raised as a sign, not a cause for the thunderbolt.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الحسين في كتاب التصفح : إن الله تعالى ما ذكر سؤال الرؤية إلا استعظمه

rows.speaker: أبو الحسين
rows.claim: Abu al-Husayn cites 4:153: the People of the Book asked for a heavenly book and then demanded sight, which God calls wrongdoing and punishes; if vision were permissible, it would be an extra miracle request.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الحسين في كتاب التصفح : إن الله تعالى ما ذكر سؤال الرؤية إلا استعظمه

rows.speaker: أبو الحسين
rows.claim: He answers that although a heavenly book is possible, the apparent wording treats both the book and seeing God as forbidden; the book’s case is set aside, leaving the sight request condemned.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الحسين في كتاب التصفح : إن الله تعالى ما ذكر سؤال الرؤية إلا استعظمه

rows.speaker: أبو الحسين
rows.claim: Abu al-Husayn also cites 25:21, where those who do not expect the meeting ask to see their Lord and are called greatly arrogant; a permissible vision request would be like asking for a dead person’s revival.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الحسين في كتاب التصفح : إن الله تعالى ما ذكر سؤال الرؤية إلا استعظمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the Muʿtazilite arguments all assume that a request for any possible thing cannot be disobedient, which does not follow from examples about food or other signs.
rows.anchor: وهو أن الرؤية لو كانت جائزة لما كان سؤالها عتوا ومنكرا / وذلك ممنوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 4:153 and 25:21 the request for vision is paired with an agreed-possible request for a book or angels, so the combined condemnation does not prove vision itself impossible.
rows.anchor: ما ذكر الرؤية إلا وذكر معها شيئا ممكنا حكمنا بجوازه بالاتفاق وهو إما نزول الكتاب من السماء أو نزول الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi rejects the claim that condemnation must mean the requested thing is impossible: the Muʿtazilites provide no proof beyond examples, which cannot establish that rule.
rows.anchor: إنك ما أقمت دليلا على أن الاستعظام لا يتحقق إلا إذا كان المطلوب ممتنعا وإنما عولت فيه على ضروب الأمثلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible reason the request was condemned is that vision of God is available only in the afterlife, making a demand for it in this world improper.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أن رؤية الله تعالى لا تحصل إلا في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that seeing God entails the end of religious obligation; on the Muʿtazilite account it brings necessary knowledge, which itself precludes obligation.
rows.anchor: أن حكم الله تعالى أن يزيل التكليف عن العبد حال ما يرى الله فكان طلب الرؤية طلبا لإزالة التكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possibility is that once proofs of the claimant are complete, demanding extra proofs is obstinacy deserving rebuke.
rows.anchor: لما تمت الدلائل على صدق المدعي كان طلب الدلائل الزائدة تعنتا والمتعنت يستوجب التعنيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth possibility is that God knows an important benefit in preventing sight in this world, just as he knows harm in sending down books or angels from heaven.
rows.anchor: لا يمتنع أن يعلم الله تعالى أن في منع الخلق عن رؤيته سبحانه في الدنيا ضربا من المصلحة المهمة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say al-ṣāʿiqah means death, citing the verse that all in heaven and earth will be struck down.
rows.anchor: الأول : أنها هي الموت وهو قول الحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi rejects the death interpretation because the Israelites could not be looking at death itself when it struck them.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : { فأخذتكم الصاعقة وأنتم تنظرون } ولو كانت الصاعقة هي الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was also described as ṣaʿiq, yet recovered; recovery is from fainting, not death.
rows.anchor: الإفاقة لا تكون عن الموت بل عن الغشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ṣāʿiqah denotes what strikes or stuns, pointing to the cause of death rather than death itself.
rows.anchor: أن الصاعقة وهي التي تصعق وذلك إشارة إلى سبب الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fact that the blow came while they watched makes the punishment more severe than if it had struck unexpectedly; the phrase emphasizes its gravity.
rows.anchor: ورابعها : أن ورودها وهم مشاهدون لها أعظم في باب العقوبة منها

rows.speaker: المحققون
rows.claim: The investigators say al-ṣāʿiqah is the cause of death, supported by the account in al-Aʿraf that calls the event a quake.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني : وهو قول المحققين : إن الصاعقة هي سبب الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three proposed causes are a fire from heaven, a cry from heaven, or God-sent hosts whose faint sound made them fall dead for a day and a night.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في أن ذلك السبب أي شيء كان على ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿth is not limited to resurrection after death; the Qur’an also says the sleepers in the cave were raised after years of sleep.
rows.anchor: لأن البعث قد ( لا ) يكون إلا بعد الموت ، كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is not included in the plural address: it is direct address to the Israelites, and his own account says he fainted and recovered, not that he died.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت : هل دخل موسى عليه السلام في هذا الكلام ؟ قلت : لا ، لوجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi rejects Ibn Qutayba’s claim that Moses died, since the verse says he recovered, a term not used for death.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة : إن موسى عليه السلام قد مات وهو خطأ لما بيناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God revived them in earthly life to impose obligations and enable belief and repentance; shukr here covers all acts of obedience.
rows.anchor: إنما بعثهم بعد الموت في دار الدنيا ليكلفهم وليتمكنوا من الإيمان ومن تلافي ما صدر عنهم من الجرائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although one might ask how the revived can be obligated when afterlife resurrection does not entail obligation, the afterlife is different: necessary knowledge of God, Paradise’s pleasures, and Hell’s pains removes obligation; these Israelites were not compelled, so their death and revival were like sleep or fainting.
rows.anchor: الذي يمنع من تكليفهم في الآخرة ليس هو الإماتة ثم الإحياء ، وإنما يمنع من ذلك

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri says God ended their lifespans with the first death and then restored them, as he restored the man by a ruined town and those who left their homes by the thousands.
rows.anchor: ونقل عن الحسن البصري أنه تعالى قطع آجالهم بهذه الإماتة ثم أعادهم كما أحيا الذي أماته حين مر على قرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi rejects that account: God had already written and announced the first death, so that was their first appointed term, and the later time was their term of life.
rows.anchor: وهذا ضعيف لأنه تعالى ما أماتهم بالصاعقة إلا وقد كتب وأخبر بذلك فصار ذلك الوقت أجلا لموتهم الأول
